title.label: A fix for what wasn’t broken; but good functionality

content.label:
Update: I was too harsh. I do like some features of Things 3. It’s much easier to move a to do item to a future date. There are still some cosmetic options I would like—lines between items, a graying out of the background for a completed task rather than just the text, keeping the title of the task visible when selecting a new date for it. But overall I like the functionality of Things 3. My opposition to design change for the sake of design change stands. 

I have loved using Things 2 for years. It was the simple, elegant to do list I need. With Things 3, once an item is checked (even accidentally), it disappears—so I am scrambling to undo if I even notice that an item is gone, or at best, I don’t see what I’ve accomplished. I liked to have a blank, checked off item that I could use as a divider between sections of my to do list—no longer possible in Things 3. There are no longer lines between items, so everything appears to have melted into one giant mass of tasks. In a to do list app, I am looking for efficiency. I am not looking for change just for the sake of change and new bells and whistles. Why not just let Things 3 users select the Things 2 interface if they prefer it?

There are a LOT of options in this space. I was an early Things adopter— it was one of the first apps I installed on my first iPhone in early 2010. I can’t say why but I the. took it upon myself to spend the decade trying dozens of alternatives. By the time I found my way back to Things, it was abundantly clear. No other productivity app even comes close. Honorable mentions for Actions (gorgeous UI on iPhone but otherwise lackluster) and OmniFocus (it goes toe-to-toe and in some cases beats Things on raw functionality, but in an unnecessarily clunky confusing interface). But there can only be one #1, and it’s never not been Things.

Seriously I feel like I’ve been missing out for a long time. OmniFocus just seems so… cluttered and poorly designed now? Things really resolves a lot of my previous pain points. Worth it!

This has so much potential but shoots itself in the foot for silly reasons. 

Sync Cloud is slow and buggy. What makes this all the more egregious is how their website goes on and on about how perfect it is and how critical it is for it to be transparent and instant. Well, hate to break it to you but it’s neither. Major fail. 

And what’s even MORE egregious is they could and should have just used iCloud sync. How tragic. I read a lot of reviews complaining about the forced upgrade being a money grab due to sync and now I must believe it to be true. 

The software would be worth every single penny they charge for every platform but if only they just saved themselves the trouble and had used iCloud sync. But I guess this would have forbade them the excuse of forcing legacy users to upgrade. Money grab gone wrong. Tragic tragic. 

Next: my calendar can sync into Things. Yay! But it doesn’t show up in the widget. What?!! 🤦🏽‍♂️ You’ve utterly destroyed the utility of calendar import. It’s invisible. It’s not playing a role in my deliverables and schedule for the day as presented by things. 

Next: managing tags is a nightmare. What horrendous usability. I can’t find a single place to easily edit them and organize them. I thought maybe the Mac version would support this but no. It’s even more limited than the iPhone app (which does offer a very hamstrung and clunky UX for tag creation and management). 

Speaking of poor tag management: Things supports creating groups of tags. Sounds great but the implementation is useless and I don’t even understand why this quarter baked idea made it out of R&D not to mention its not at all supported on the Mac version. 

All this just from one hour of using both apps. The promise is huge. No doubt. But the execution at this time is extremely flawed and it seems to me the reason was some bean counter chose to force the team to reinvent the cloud so they could extent leverage and hijack legacy users for money. Quite likely they will end up charging to use their proprietary cloud sync some day to grab even more cash from their locked in user base. 

But the product suffers greatly because resources were allocated on the wrong things.

I’m open to updating my review should they come to their senses.

title.label: Quite usable and functional but with some key limitations

content.label: The main one for me: Tags are contexts. They are visible per item in an item list on the mac but not mobile. Yes you can filter a view by tags but visually they are mostly hidden in mobile. Since tags are how GTD contexts are implemented in Things, this proves to be a major handicap. The implementation is much more effective on the Mac, and there’s no reason mobile couldn’t expose tags more obviously.
